reads: the capability table as the worktree holds it and at each commit that changed it: the capability id of each table row, by the row's line

examples.named: defect of the old reader: its pattern gave a row an id only where the row's first cell opens with the code span, a rule of its own for what a capability row is. The rows of the table's first section name the capability in words before the code span (`Kernel event loop (`kernel.event-loop`)`; twelve rows of the table as the worktree holds it, where the base's pattern reads 37 rows and the worktree's reader 49), so the history repair read no id from those and, by the base's source, refused to restore an edited one; the dated rows under them open with the code span and both readers read them. The planning subject at the base read the id anywhere in the first cell, and the worktree's one row reader does. Every id the base read stands at the same line; the rows gained are those whose first cell holds text before its code span
